tarife.despreProiectText: Opened in 2008, Telegondola Piatra Neamț is one of the city's most important tourism investments. Built by the Austrian company Doppelmayr, it links the city centre with the Cozla plateau and gives a full panorama of Piatra Neamț, Lake Bâtca Doamnei and the mountains around it. More than a million passengers have ridden it so far, which speaks for the value and durability of the project.

despre.calatorieText: The Piatra Neamț cable car gives you a wide view of the city and the countryside around it. The route starts from the station next to the railway station and climbs to the Cozla plateau, 632 metres above sea level. On the way up the view changes little by little, from the historic centre and the city's buildings to the parks and the wooded slopes of the mountain. The ride takes a few minutes and is calm and safe, on a modern, environmentally friendly transport system. At the top you can take in a 360° panorama of the whole city, Lake Bâtca Doamnei and Mount Ceahlău. It is one of the best-loved experiences in the area, for visitors and locals alike.
despre.traseuText: From the cable car you can see every detail of the city. The route starts in the centre and climbs towards the Cozla plateau, giving you a full picture of the streets, buildings and green spaces. As the cabin rises, the city settles more clearly into the landscape, and the contrast between built-up and green areas shows how well balanced the place is. At the top the view takes in everything and explains why Piatra Neamț is counted among the most beautiful cities in Romania.
despre.valoriSubtitlu: The principles that guide us every day

siguranta.text: Every ride is closely monitored and kept to the highest technical standards. Passenger safety comes first and is the basis of the trust people place in us.

colaborare.text: We rely on team spirit and cooperation. Every employee, partner and visitor helps keep a system that runs efficiently and fairly, for everyone's benefit.

inovatie.text: We keep updating our technology and the way we operate to offer a modern, sustainable experience that fits today's needs. We respect tradition, but always look ahead.

experienta.text: We focus on our visitors' comfort and satisfaction. We want every ride to be pleasant, easy and memorable, and Piatra Neamț to be discovered at its best.

despre.misiuneText: We want to give visitors a genuine experience of Piatra Neamț seen from above, where the city meets nature. Every ride is an invitation to explore, made safely and with care for the environment. We hope each trip leaves good memories and a deeper connection with the landscape, culture and spirit of this place.
despre.viziuneText: We aim to become the most appreciated and sustainable cable transport system in Romania, known for professionalism, safety and respect for the environment. We believe a simple ride up can change the way you see the city and the nature around it. Through innovation, attention to detail and local involvement, we want to establish Piatra Neamț as a leading destination for responsible and educational tourism in Romania.
despre.povesteSubtitlu: A journey built on vision, passion and perseverance

BisericaSfIoan.t02: The Church of the Nativity of St John the Baptist
BisericaSfIoan.t05: Built in 1497–1498, the Church of the Nativity of St John the Baptist is one of the oldest and most valuable buildings in Piatra Neamț. Founded by Stephen the Great as part of the Princely Court, it is a landmark of the mature Moldavian style, influenced by Gothic architecture.
BisericaSfIoan.t07: The building is made of stone and brick, with refined decorative elements: a twisted cable moulding, blind niches, buttresses and glazed ceramics on the façades. The church has a mixed plan, with side apses built into the walls and an inner vault supported by hemispherical domes set in a row.
BisericaSfIoan.t09: Green and yellow ceramic discs on the façade
BisericaSfIoan.t15: The church within the Princely Court
BisericaSfIoan.t16: The church was where the ruler and his court came to pray, as an integral part of the princely residence. Over the centuries it has been carefully restored, keeping its original form and materials.

CasaIonCreanga.t04: In Humulești, on the edge of Târgu Neamț, stands the modest house where Ion Creangă, one of Romania's best-loved storytellers, was born and grew up. Built in 1833 from wooden beams and roofed with shingles, it was carefully kept by the family's descendants until 1959 and is now a memorial museum visited by tens of thousands of people every year.
CasaIonCreanga.t07: In the two rooms and the low entrance hall you'll find the world of Nică's childhood: Smaranda's dowry chest, the wooden baby tub, the spinning wheel, the hearth and the stove ledge he held on to while learning to walk.
CasaIonCreanga.t08: On the table are the writer's bust and the prayer book he learned to read from, and in the pantry you can see where he hid the famous hoopoe from the linden tree.
CasaIonCreanga.t10: Next to the house lies the "Ion Creangă" Theme Park, where the characters from his stories come to life – the goat and her three kids, the bear tricked by the fox, Smărăndița and Moș Chiorpec.
CasaIonCreanga.t11: A charming place where real life and childhood meet, so that visitors of all ages can rediscover the joy of dreaming.

CetateaNeamt.t04: High above Târgu Neamț, on a rocky ridge, Neamț Citadel has watched over the Ozana valley for more than six centuries. Built at the end of the 14th century and strengthened by Stephen the Great with taller walls, bastions and a deep defensive moat, the fortress turned back invaders time and again.
CetateaNeamt.t05: Legends were born here — from "The Mother of Stephen the Great" to the famous stand of the local mountain guards against Sobieski.
CetateaNeamt.t08: The citadel has been restored and is open to visitors. You cross the bridge resting on 11 stone pillars, walk in under the Gothic gate and discover the inner courtyard, the chapel, the armoury, the dungeon and rooms furnished as they once were.
CetateaNeamt.t09: The bonus? A breathtaking view over the Ozana, the river Creangă called "the beautifully flowing one", and the Neamț mountains.

CheileBicazului.t04: On the border between Neamț and Harghita counties, in the heart of the Hășmaș Mountains, lies one of Romania's most spectacular natural sights. Bicaz Gorge was cut by the Bicaz River through Jurassic limestone, and the road winds between huge rock walls, tunnels, caves and dizzying hairpin bends.
CheileBicazului.t05: Every bend brings you closer to nature, to quiet and to the Carpathians at their most dramatic. The scenery here is so striking it takes your breath away.
CheileBicazului.t09: The natural symbol of the gorge, a huge arch shaped in the rock by the forces of nature. It is the area's best-known landmark and the perfect spot for memorable photos.
CheileBicazului.t11: A vertical wall more than 300 metres high, a favourite with climbers from all over the country. If you prefer to keep your feet on the ground, the view from below is just as impressive.
CheileBicazului.t13: The narrowest and most dramatic stretch of the road, where the rock walls seem to close in overhead. This is where you really feel how vast the mountains are.
CheileBicazului.t15: At the upper end of the gorge lies Red Lake, a natural lake formed by a landslide in 1837. The tree trunks rising out of the water give it a unique, almost unreal look.
CheileBicazului.t19: Wild mountain trails along the tributaries of the Bicaz River, for anyone who wants to explore beyond the main road. Here you will find complete peace and untamed nature.
CheileBicazului.t21: <span1>•</span1><span2>Hiking on marked trails of varying difficulty</span2>
CheileBicazului.t27: The gorge is crossed by national road DN12C, which links the towns of Bicaz (Neamț) and Gheorgheni (Harghita). The road is fully paved and spectacular in every season.
CheileBicazului.t33: Bicaz Gorge – Hășmaș National Park is a nature reserve of national importance, so the area is protected and visitors are asked to follow the rules for behaving in nature.
CheileBicazului.t34: Along the road you will find rest areas, stalls selling local produce (cheese, honey, handicrafts) and safe viewpoints for visitors.

CurteaDomneasca.t02: The Princely Court and Stephen the Great's Tower
CurteaDomneasca.t05: In the centre of Piatra Neamț stands one of the most valuable medieval ensembles in Romania. Built between 1497 and 1499 during the reign of Stephen the Great, the Princely Court served as a royal residence, an administrative centre and a place of defence.
CurteaDomneasca.t06: The Princely Court – the ruler's residence
CurteaDomneasca.t07: The complex was built between 1497 and 1499 on a terrace of the Bistrița river. It originally included the princely palace, the court church and household buildings, all surrounded by fortified walls.
CurteaDomneasca.t08: What has survived to this day:
CurteaDomneasca.t09: The Church of the Nativity of St John the Baptist (1497–1498)
CurteaDomneasca.t11: The outline of the original fortifications in the square
CurteaDomneasca.t17: Built in 1499, right after the victory at Codrii Cosminului. Made of rough stone and brick, it rises 19 metres, supported by four buttresses.

DealulCozla.t06: Rising over the northern part of Piatra Neamț, Cozla Mountain is one of the most characteristic natural and cultural places in the area. Part of the Stânișoara Mountains, the last step of the Eastern Carpathians, Cozla offers spectacular views over the city and the whole Bistrița valley.
DealulCozla.t08: For centuries the foot of the mountain was home to the old “Târgul Pietrei” market town, where Stephen the Great chose to build the Princely Court. It was also the site of a Cucuteni settlement, the highest known settlement of this culture in Moldavia.
DealulCozla.t09: In the late 19th century Cozla became a well-known destination thanks to its mineral springs, praised and awarded at the 1900 Paris World Exhibition.
DealulCozla.t11: After the natural disaster of 1897, when torrential rain caused massive landslides, mayor Nicu Albu started a large afforestation campaign. Hundreds of people planted firs and pines brought from Sinaia, turning Cozla into the park it is today.
DealulCozla.t12: “It was hard, but we defeated nature” – Nicu Albu, 1904
DealulCozla.t16: Discovered in 1882, the sodium chloride and sulphurous mineral waters turned the city into a spa resort, officially recognised in 1889.
DealulCozla.t18: Romania's first Oligocene fossil fish were discovered here between 1883 and 1885. It was declared a palaeontological reserve in 1971.
DealulCozla.t20: A unique geological reserve: formations known as “aeolian potholes”, round hollows carved by the wind into hard rock over thousands of years.
DealulCozla.t22: Cozla Mountain is the city's main place for leisure and adventure:
DealulCozla.t30: Views towards Ceahlău and Lake Bâtca Doamnei
DealulCozla.t31: “A place where history, science and nature meet in harmony – Cozla Mountain is, without doubt, the green heart of Piatra Neamț.”

GradinNicuAlbu.t01: Nicu Albu Public Garden, Piatra Neamț
GradinNicuAlbu.t03: At the foot of Cozla Hill
GradinNicuAlbu.t06: A new green space in the heart of the city
GradinNicuAlbu.t07: The newest place to relax in Piatra Neamț, the “Nicu Albu” Public Garden gives back to the city a site of historical and symbolic value: the former zoo. At the foot of Cozla Hill, the garden links the city centre with the mountain trails and is open to the community, to art and to nature.
GradinNicuAlbu.t08: A place of memory and renewal
GradinNicuAlbu.t09: The urban regeneration project combines respect for the past with contemporary technology and design, keeping the memory of the old zoo alive through reinterpreted architectural elements:
GradinNicuAlbu.t10: The former bear enclosure has become a metal art installation – a stylised silhouette that recalls the history of the place
GradinNicuAlbu.t11: The fence of the former lion enclosure now surrounds a platform for temporary exhibitions
GradinNicuAlbu.t12: The central lake has been reshaped into a reflecting pool that mirrors the greenery and the light, the park's main attraction
GradinNicuAlbu.t13: A legacy dedicated to Nicu Albu
GradinNicuAlbu.t14: The garden bears the name of the city's most visionary mayor, Nicu N. Albu (1853–1908) – mayor, prefect, senator and one of the great modernisers of Piatra Neamț. In the early 20th century he laid the foundations of the modern city: water and sewage networks, the development of Cozla, the first modern schools and the afforestation of the mountain.
GradinNicuAlbu.t17: The new public garden is designed as a multi-purpose space where nature, culture and meeting people come together naturally:
GradinNicuAlbu.t19: For summer concerts, film screenings and cultural events
GradinNicuAlbu.t21: Spaces for creative work and art exhibitions
GradinNicuAlbu.t23: A café, flower shop and place to relax in one
GradinNicuAlbu.t25: For children, designed for different age groups
GradinNicuAlbu.t27: Chess tables and benches for reading
GradinNicuAlbu.t29: Turns the garden into a visual show in the evening
GradinNicuAlbu.t30: “In the shadow of Cozla, where the zoo once stood, a garden for people is born again – a place of joy, art and memory.”
GradinNicuAlbu.t33: The “Nicu Albu” Public Garden is a lively space for relaxation, creativity and cultural events. The place where the past meets the future.

LaculBatcaDoamnei.t06: A natural gem at the foot of the city, where the calm water meets the striking outline of Mount Ceahlău and the panorama of the city below. Lake Bâtca Doamnei is where the quiet waters of the Bistrița meet the high Carpathian sky.
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t07: A natural gem at the foot of the city
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t08: Created in 1962 by damming the Bistrița River, the lake protects the area from floods and is also valuable for tourism and wildlife. It is part of the same river system as the Izvorul Muntelui–Bicaz Dam.
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t09: Covering 235 hectares and up to 15.5 metres deep, Bâtca Doamnei is one of the largest reservoirs in the Moldavia region.
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t18: Although it is man-made, Bâtca Doamnei has become a living ecosystem over time. It is part of the chain of lakes that forms the eastern Carpathian migration corridor, together with the Vaduri and Pângărați lakes. The area matters a great deal for preserving biodiversity and natural habitats in Eastern Europe.
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t19: Migratory birds in the cold season:
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t26: Birdwatching is becoming more and more popular here, and the lake now draws ornithologists and nature photographers.
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t29: Near the lake rises Bâtca Doamnei Hill, home to the ruins of the Dacian fortress of Petrodava, one of the most important strongholds of the free Dacians east of the Carpathians.
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t30: Here nature, history and the spirit of the place come together in a single landscape.
LaculBatcaDoamnei.t32: A great place to relax, walk along the shore, take photos or try gentle water sports. From the northern shore you look out over Piatra Neamț, and to the west towards Ceahlău and the Stânișoara Mountains.

LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t04: The largest reservoir in Romania's mountains: about 32.6 km² stretching over 35 kilometres, with wide views and Ceahlău as a constant backdrop. The Bicaz Dam is an impressive 127 metres high, and the road across its crest offers photogenic hairpin bends on the DN15.
LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t05: Where mountains, water and stories meet. You come for the scenery and stay for the peace.
LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t09: Cruises from Bicaz Port to the Poiana Largului viaduct, kayaking and SUP in the calm of the morning, and fishing with a permit (trout, chub, nase).
LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t11: Hikes to viewpoints, climbs up Ceahlău from Durău, and cycling along the DN15 with stops in bays and villages.
LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t13: The dam crest in the morning, the quiet bays at Izvorul Alb, sunset from Bicaz Port with Ceahlău behind, and the Poiana Largului viaduct.
LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t15: By car: DN15 Piatra Neamț → Bicaz → along the lake to Poiana Largului. From Transylvania: DN12C through Bicaz Gorge.
LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t16: By train: to Bicaz station, then a 5-minute taxi ride to the dam/port.
LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t21: Winter: spectacular scenery, fewer activities on the water

LaculIzvorulMuntelui.t25: • The midday wind whips up waves – go out on the water in the morning

LaculRosu.t03: The natural treasure of the Hășmaș Mountains
LaculRosu.t04: Set at the foot of Hășmașul Mare, at an altitude of almost 1,000 metres, Red Lake is one of the most spectacular natural lakes in Romania. It was formed by a landslide in 1838 and is surrounded by conifer forests and towering cliffs, serving as the gateway to Bicaz Gorge.
LaculRosu.t05: A place where nature, legend and quiet come together in a living picture of the Eastern Carpathians.
LaculRosu.t07: Red Lake – tree trunks in the water
LaculRosu.t08: <strong1>The largest natural dam lake in the country</strong1>, covering almost 12 hectares. Petrified fir trunks rise out of the water, silent witnesses of the forest swallowed up nearly two centuries ago.
LaculRosu.t09: Its name comes from the <strong1>reddish water</strong1>, coloured by iron oxides in the soil, and from the legend of a whole village said to have been swallowed by the mountain.
LaculRosu.t10: In Hungarian it is known as <strong1>Gyilkos-tó</strong1> (“Killer Lake”), a name that keeps alive the dramatic story of how it was formed.
LaculRosu.t13: Glide between the submerged tree trunks and enjoy the scenery from a unique angle. It is a calming and slightly surreal experience.
LaculRosu.t15: Trails lead to Bicaz Gorge, Poiana Ghilcoș, Altar Rock or Suhardul Mic. There is something for every fitness level, from gentle walks to more demanding hikes.
LaculRosu.t17: In the morning, when the mist lifts off the surface of the lake, is the perfect time for spectacular photos. The light plays beautifully among the trunks.
LaculRosu.t30: The Red Lake area has a therapeutic microclimate, good for relaxation, insomnia and stress. The clean air, rich in forest aerosols, and the complete quiet make it a perfect place to recharge.
LaculRosu.t32: It offers plenty of accommodation, local food and outdoor activities. It is an ideal starting point for exploring Bicaz Gorge and the Hășmaș Mountains.
LaculRosu.t34: Red Lake lies on national road DN12C, which crosses Bicaz Gorge and links the towns of Bicaz and Gheorgheni.
LaculRosu.t36: Drive to Bicaz, then take the DN12C through Bicaz Gorge. The total distance is about 60 km, and it is worth stopping in the gorge for photos.
LaculRosu.t38: 26 km on the DN12C, a spectacular mountain route.
LaculRosu.t39: Tip: Stop at Bicaz Gorge on your way to the lake for the full experience.
LaculRosu.t42: The lake is spectacular in every season: summer for boat trips, autumn for the forest colours reflected in the water, winter for the frozen landscape.
LaculRosu.t45: • Layered clothing, it can be chilly
LaculRosu.t47: • Water and snacks for longer trails
LaculRosu.t48: Important: Respect nature and leave no trace. Help keep this place beautiful for future generations.
LaculRosu.t51: After exploring Red Lake and Bicaz Gorge, continue your adventure with the Piatra Neamț cable car for another spectacular view of the region

ManastireaAgapia.t06: Agapia Monastery is one of the largest convents in Romania, founded by Hetman Gavriil Coci (1641–1643). It is famous for the murals painted by Nicolae Grigorescu between 1858 and 1861, considered a masterpiece of Romanian art.
ManastireaAgapia.t10: Hetman Gavriil Coci, brother of Prince Vasile Lupu (1641–1643)
ManastireaAgapia.t12: Holy Archangels Michael and Gabriel (8 November)
ManastireaAgapia.t14: A convent of ≈300–400 nuns, one of the largest in Romania
ManastireaAgapia.t16: Triconch plan, stone and brick walls; neoclassical style with an octagonal tower; a square enclosure with wooden porches and a bell tower from 1823

ManastireaAgapia.t23: Metropolitan Veniamin Costache, Nicolae Grigorescu, Ion Creangă, Alexandru Vlahuță, Calistrat Hogaș
ManastireaAgapia.t25: The monastery is home to the "St. Parascheva" Monastic Theological Seminary – the only seminary for girls in Moldavia, carrying on the settlement's tradition of education and spirituality.

ManastireaBistrita.t06: Bistrița Monastery is a major landmark of Moldavian spirituality, founded by Prince Alexander the Good in 1402. The impressive ensemble includes the princely church, a bell tower, a chapel and a museum with treasures and manuscripts of priceless value.

ManastireaNeamt.t06: Neamț Monastery is the largest and oldest monastic settlement in Moldavia. Its beginnings go back to the 14th century, and the present church was raised by Stephen the Great at the end of the 15th century. It is a symbol of Moldavian spirituality and of Orthodox Christian continuity.
ManastireaNeamt.t10: Beginnings in the 14th century (Peter I Mușat); present church – Stephen the Great, late 15th century
ManastireaNeamt.t12: The Ascension of the Lord (40 days after Easter)

ManastireaPangarati.t06: Pângărați Monastery was founded in 1560 by Prince Alexandru Lăpușneanu. It is a place of prayer and spirituality with a unique architecture: a princely church with two altars, one above the other, and a chapel in the basement that once served as a hiding place.

ManastireaSecu.t06: Secu Monastery, founded in 1602 by the high steward Nestor Ureche, is an old religious settlement in the Neamț region, built on the site of the “Hermitage of Zosim”. With its fortified architecture and scholarly tradition, the monastery combines community life with the spiritual heritage of Moldavia.
ManastireaSecu.t10: High steward Nestor Ureche (1602), on the site of the “Hermitage of Zosim”
ManastireaSecu.t12: The Beheading of St John the Baptist (29 August)

ManastireaSihastria.t06: Sihăstria Monastery, founded in 1655 by the hermit Atanasie, is a centre of Romanian hesychasm. It is known as the resting place of the great spiritual father Cleopa Ilie and as an important place of pilgrimage and spiritual retreat.

ManastireaSihla.t06: Sihla Hermitage stands at an altitude of about 1,000 m on the Sihla ridge (Stânișoara Mountains), on the site of the hermitage where St Teodora of Sihla lived. Regarded as “ground hallowed by the prayers of hermits”, it is a place of silence and prayer among forests of stone.

ManastireaSihla.t12: The Nativity of St John the Baptist (old church) and the Transfiguration (6 August)

ManastireaVaratec.t06: Văratec Monastery is the largest convent in Romania, home to more than 400 nuns. It was founded in 1785 under the guidance of Paisius Velichkovsky. The resting place of Veronica Micle and Safta Brâncoveanu, the monastery is a symbol of Moldavian spirituality and culture.

MasivulCeahlau.t04: Ceahlău wins you over with its simplicity and grandeur. Climb it patiently and it rewards you at every step with spectacular scenery, fresh air and breathtaking views.
MasivulCeahlau.t08: Ocolașul Mare (1,907 m) and Toaca (1,904 m), with views stretching to Izvorul Muntelui Lake and the Hășmaș Mountains. Sunrise on Toaca is unforgettable.
MasivulCeahlau.t10: Panaghia, Piatra Ciobanului, Scaunele Zeilor – formations that look as if they were carved to impress.
MasivulCeahlau.t12: A drop of about 30 metres on the Rupturilor Valley, a must-see stop on the trails around Durău.
MasivulCeahlau.t14: Spruce and fir forests, alpine meadows, chamois and capercaillie. Ceahlău is part of Ceahlău National Park (7,742 hectares), a protected area with strict rules for behaving in nature.
MasivulCeahlau.t17: The scenery changes every 30–40 minutes, from dense forest to open meadows and then alpine ridges. The trails are well marked and maintained.
MasivulCeahlau.t19: Clean air, cool summers and vivid colours in autumn. In October the forest turns into a palette of yellow, orange and red.
MasivulCeahlau.t21: The tale of Baba Dochia and the “pyramid” of light at the Feast of the Transfiguration – local legends add charm to the experience. Ceahlău is not just a mountain, it is a symbol.
MasivulCeahlau.t30: • Izvorul Muntelui – the chalet of the same name
MasivulCeahlau.t41: Note: Times are a guide for hikers with average experience. Allow extra time for breaks and photos.
MasivulCeahlau.t44: More settled weather, good visibility and all trails open. Summer is cool at the top, perfect for hiking.
MasivulCeahlau.t46: Autumn colours turn the forest into a visual feast. It is photographers' favourite time of year.
MasivulCeahlau.t48: Only with full winter gear and mountain experience. Snow can be deep, visibility poor and there is a risk of avalanches.
MasivulCeahlau.t51: Follow the trail markings, leave no trace and don't feed the animals. There is an access fee and park rules apply – ask at the entry points.
MasivulCeahlau.t58: Important: Tell someone which trail you are taking and when you expect to be back. Your safety comes first.
MasivulCeahlau.t59: “Ceahlău wins you over with its simplicity and grandeur. Climb it patiently and it rewards you at every step.”

MuntelePietricica.t06: The stone symbol of Piatra Neamț, Pietricica Mountain rises to a maximum altitude of 590 m. It dominates the southern part of the city and offers one of the finest views over the Bistrița valley and the surrounding mountains.
MuntelePietricica.t08: Pietricica Mountain is a unique geological relic, the remnant of an overturned fold formed in the Palaeogene, which preserves Oligocene layers rich in fossil deposits.
MuntelePietricica.t09: Scientifically, it is a true natural archive of the geological history of the Eastern Carpathians.
MuntelePietricica.t10: Over time Pietricica has been seen as a defining landmark of the city's identity – many researchers even believe that the name “Piatra” (“the Stone”) comes from this rocky massif, visible from every corner of the town.
MuntelePietricica.t12: Although its altitude is modest, the view from the top of Pietricica is spectacular: Ceahlău Mountain, the Bistrița valley, lakes Bâtca Doamnei and Reconstrucția, as well as the Cozla, Cernegura and Cârloman hills.
MuntelePietricica.t13: At sunset a special light colours the city and the mountains in warm tones, making any visit memorable.
MuntelePietricica.t17: A small cave cut into the rock on the slope facing the Bistrița, said to have been a retreat for hermits. A place full of mystery and spirituality.
MuntelePietricica.t19: According to tradition, this is where the border guards lit fires to warn of approaching danger. A strategic point with deep historical meaning.
MuntelePietricica.t21: Once described as a “harsh and bare” mountain, Pietricica has been largely reforested in recent decades, and today its paths offer gentle walks, viewpoints and natural shelters.
MuntelePietricica.t23: By car almost up to the plateau
MuntelePietricica.t31: A place for hiking, relaxing and photography, Pietricica Mountain is the perfect complement to the urban experience of Piatra Neamț.
MuntelePietricica.t37: Nature and quiet close to the city
MuntelePietricica.t38: “Visitors who climb to the top discover not only a wide view over the city, but also the essence of the bond between stone, history and people. It is, without doubt, one of the finest viewpoints in the whole of Neamț County.”
MuntelePietricica.t40: Take the cable car and look down on the city's stone symbol

MuzeulCalistratHogas.t01: Calistrat Hogaș Memorial Museum, Piatra Neamț
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t06: The house where the life and work of the writer Calistrat Hogaș (1847–1917) found their permanent home. It keeps his furniture, library, manuscripts, photographs and personal belongings, in a house built in the style of a late 19th-century Moldavian market town.
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t08: Calistrat Hogaș settled in Piatra Neamț in 1869, ran the local secondary school and built both his family life and his writing here. The house was rebuilt in 1880 and became a memorial museum in 1969, thanks to a donation from Sidonia C. Hogaș, the writer's daughter.
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t10: The writer's study with original objects and manuscripts
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t13: A townhouse interior from around 1900, fully preserved
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t16: Inside the museum – the writer's study
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t17: Calistrat Hogaș (1847–1917) began teaching in Piatra Neamț in 1869 and returned as headmaster in 1870–1871. He married here and stayed connected to the town all his life, and his writings about journeys through Neamț and Ceahlău made his name.
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t21: Marries and settles here for good
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t22: Writes "În munții Neamțului" (In the Neamț Mountains) and other works
MuzeulCalistratHogas.t36: Carry on exploring with a walk through the old town, then take the cable car to see Piatra Neamț just as Calistrat Hogaș described it

MuzeulCucuteni.t01: Cucuteni Eneolithic Art Museum, Piatra Neamț
MuzeulCucuteni.t06: Home to one of the most valuable collections of prehistoric art in Europe, devoted to the Cucuteni culture – the most brilliant Eneolithic civilisation in what is now Romania and one of the oldest in the world.
MuzeulCucuteni.t08: The museum opened on 24 June 2005, Piatra Neamț's City Day, marking 120 years since the discovery of the site that gave the Cucuteni culture its name. It is a landmark achievement for Romanian archaeology and culture.
MuzeulCucuteni.t18: The building is listed as a historic monument and stands in the heart of the old town, next to the Princely Court. Built in 1928–1930 by the architect Roger Bolomey, the five-storey building is considered one of the most elegant pieces of architecture in Piatra Neamț.
MuzeulCucuteni.t21: Originally: Petrodava Bank (the first private bank)
MuzeulCucuteni.t22: Later: branch of the National Bank of Romania
MuzeulCucuteni.t39: Combine the museum with a walk through the old town, taking in the Princely Court and the other museums. Just a short walk away you can catch the Telegondola Piatra Neamț for a sweeping view of the land where the Cucuteni culture came to life

MuzeulDeArta.t06: A cultural landmark in the heart of the old town, within the grounds of the Princely Court. The Piatra Neamț Art Museum offers an elegant journey through the development of Romanian visual art, from classical to contemporary.
MuzeulDeArta.t08: The art collection goes back to the work of Father Constantin Matasă (1878–1971), founder of the Archaeological Museum. In 1960, with the support of the painter Iulia Hălăucescu, an Art Section was set up. In 1980 it became an institution in its own right.
MuzeulDeArta.t18: The building was put up in 1930 as the "Lascăr Catargi" Boys' Primary School No. 1, designed by the architects Roger Bolomey and Fr. Droz. Its architecture blends traditional Moldavian features with modern interwar details.
MuzeulDeArta.t49: Explore the whole Princely Court area – St John's Princely Church, Stephen the Great's Tower and the Cucuteni Museum. And for a complete panorama of the city, ride the Telegondola Piatra Neamț

MuzeulDeEtnografie.t06: A place devoted to the traditional culture and authentic crafts of the Neamț area. The Ethnography Museum takes you into the village life of old Romania, through objects, costumes, symbols and stories that have been carefully preserved.
MuzeulDeEtnografie.t08: The ethnography collection began to take shape in the mid-20th century, following research by a team led by Romulus Vuia when the Bicaz dam was being built. The museum officially opened in 1980, in a building that perfectly reflects the spirit of folk tradition.
MuzeulDeEtnografie.t18: The current building dates from 1924, when it was built as the home of the head of the "Lascăr Catargi" Primary School, to a design by the architect Eugen Albu. It is a remarkable example of the Neo-Romanian style, with details that recall traditional houses.
MuzeulDeEtnografie.t30: • The collection expanded by Dr Elena Florescu
MuzeulDeEtnografie.t49: Include the Ethnography Museum in a cultural tour of the Princely Court, together with the other museums. End your visit with a Telegondola ride for a spectacular view of the Bistrița Valley – the landscape that shaped the region's whole folk culture

MuzeulIstorieArheologie.t01: Museum of History and Archaeology, Piatra Neamț
MuzeulIstorieArheologie.t06: The leading institution for the historical and archaeological heritage of the Neamț area. The main exhibition traces how human communities in the region developed, alongside the coin collection, temporary exhibition spaces and a virtual tour.
MuzeulIstorieArheologie.t08: Local museum work began in the first quarter of the 20th century. In 1934, at the initiative of the priest Constantin Matasă, an archaeological museum devoted to local finds took shape. Since 1980 the museum has been housed in the historic building at 10 Mihai Eminescu Street.
MuzeulIstorieArheologie.t10: Main exhibition with archaeological and historical pieces
MuzeulIstorieArheologie.t18: The permanent exhibition shows how human communities in the Neamț area evolved, from prehistory to modern times. It was last reorganised in 2007–2008, with the reopening scheduled for 15 May 2025.
MuzeulIstorieArheologie.t41: Combine the museum with a walk around town that takes in the Princely Court, Stephen the Great's Tower and the Wooden Synagogue. For a view over the whole city, ride the Telegondola Piatra Neamț

MuzeulStiinte.t06: A journey through the history of the Earth and of life. The Natural Sciences Museum in Piatra Neamț is devoted to studying, preserving and sharing the natural heritage of Neamț County, a region known for its rich geology, fossils, plants and wildlife.
MuzeulStiinte.t08: Founded on 1 September 1960, the museum was conceived as an institution for studying and preserving the natural heritage of Neamț County.
MuzeulStiinte.t09: In 1961 the historian Iulian Antonescu and his wife, the teacher Eugenia Antonescu, donated the building that still houses the museum today, so that it could become a place of science education for the public.
MuzeulStiinte.t10: Officially opened on 15 November 1969, the museum was regarded from the start as a model of Romanian museum practice.
MuzeulStiinte.t12: 1980: The permanent exhibition is completely redone
MuzeulStiinte.t13: 1992–1993: The striking prehistoric landscapes are created
MuzeulStiinte.t18: Visitors can set off on a fascinating journey through the history of the Earth:
MuzeulStiinte.t20: Room 1: How the Earth's crust evolved – plate tectonics and geological processes
MuzeulStiinte.t21: Rooms 2–3: How life evolved across the geological eras – dioramas and reconstructions of the prehistoric world
MuzeulStiinte.t22: Fossil collections: Famous Oligocene fish fossils, unique in Europe
MuzeulStiinte.t23: Local plants and wildlife: Neamț's biodiversity, from mountain forests to aquatic ecosystems
MuzeulStiinte.t24: Finds from the Cozla–Pietricica–Cernegura area make this museum a scientific reference point in Europe.
MuzeulStiinte.t27: The journal "Studii și cercetări" – an annual scientific publication
MuzeulStiinte.t29: Educational workshops and themed events for schoolchildren
MuzeulStiinte.t31: Programmes to protect and conserve biodiversity
MuzeulStiinte.t45: The Natural Sciences Museum is more than a place of science: it is a journey through the history of the Earth and of life, in the heart of one of Romania's most beautiful mountain towns.

ParculCentral.t03: Youth Park / Stephen the Great Park
ParculCentral.t07: The green heart of the city
ParculCentral.t08: Central Park is where city life meets history, culture and everyday relaxation. Also known as “Youth Park” and “Stephen the Great Park”, it is one of the most popular places for a stroll in town.
ParculCentral.t11: Right next to the Princely Court and Stephen the Great's Tower, the park marks the symbolic link between Moldavia's princely past and the modern feel of today's city. From here you can take in, at a single glance, the most important monuments of the old centre of Piatra Neamț.
ParculCentral.t19: Throughout the year the park is the community's main meeting place:
ParculCentral.t21: Spectacular decorations, fairy lights and a festive atmosphere turn the park into a magical place.
ParculCentral.t22: New Year's Eve in the centre
ParculCentral.t23: The New Year's party brings thousands of people together for fireworks and celebration.
ParculCentral.t25: Concerts, exhibitions, festivals and pedestrian areas at weekends for relaxing and meeting friends.
ParculCentral.t27: With wide alleys, well-kept lawns, places to rest and an elegant urban setting, Central Park is the perfect place for a quiet break between two sights or an evening stroll under the city's warm lights.
ParculCentral.t28: Walks and relaxing in the open air
ParculCentral.t32: “Whether you come to admire Stephen the Great's Tower, see a show at the Youth Theatre or simply enjoy the fresh air, Central Park is the soul of Piatra Neamț.”
ParculCentral.t34: After your walk in the park, take the cable car and admire the whole city from above

RezervatiaZimbri.t03: Meet the giants of the Carpathians
RezervatiaZimbri.t04: Here you can see the mighty European bison (Bison bonasus) – a symbol of the Carpathians, successfully brought back to Neamț – in a controlled habitat and, more and more often, in the wild. The setting is generous: 11,500 hectares of forests and clearings north of Vânători-Neamț, home also to bears, red deer and roe deer.
RezervatiaZimbri.t05: Come with patience and leave with stories.
RezervatiaZimbri.t08: Safe for families with children. Watch bison up close as they graze and rest.
RezervatiaZimbri.t10: Guided tours and observation from a distance. A real chance to spot bison roaming through the forest.
RezervatiaZimbri.t12: <span1>•</span1><span2>Wildlife watching at sunrise/sunset (soft light, active animals)</span2>
RezervatiaZimbri.t13: <span1>•</span1><span2>Walks through clearings with ponds (Bison, Red Deer and Roe Deer ponds)</span2>
RezervatiaZimbri.t14: <span1>•</span1><span2>Nature photography: tree lines, morning mist, bison silhouettes</span2>

SinagogaBaalSemTov.t01: Baal Shem Tov Wooden Synagogue, Piatra Neamț
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t05: At 7 Dimitrie Ernici Street, in the old town of Piatra Neamț, the Baal Shem Tov Wooden Synagogue is one of the oldest and most valuable Jewish places of worship in Eastern Europe. Built in 1766 on the site of an earlier synagogue dating from before 1497, it is considered the oldest fully preserved synagogue in Romania.
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t07: The building is made entirely of massive wooden beams resting on a high stone foundation. You enter by going down a few steps, a feature typical of traditional synagogues in Central and Eastern Europe.
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t10: The ritual curtain from 1767, with Hebrew inscriptions
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t15: Inside the synagogue, with the Holy Ark
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t16: The present synagogue was built under a charter signed on 19 July 1766 by Prince Grigore III Ghica. Over time it went through several restorations, the most recent between 2004 and 2009.
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t21: Support: World Monuments Fund, New York
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t22: A working monument open to visitors
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t24: <span1>•</span1><span2>Massive wooden beams on a stone foundation</span2>
SinagogaBaalSemTov.t35: Discover the Princely Court and Stephen the Great's Tower, just a few minutes' walk away, then take the cable car to see the city from above

StadionulCeahlau.t06: Ceahlăul Stadium is the most important sports complex in Neamț County and a symbol of sporting passion and achievement in Piatra Neamț. The arena is approved for international competitions, including national team and Champions League matches.
StadionulCeahlau.t08: With 14,000 seats and modern facilities, the complex has a main pitch with undersoil heating, two covered stands, floodlights, a training base, auxiliary pitches and space for accommodation and sports recovery.
StadionulCeahlau.t19: Founded in 1919, the Ceahlăul Sports Club is one of the oldest and most respected sports institutions in Moldavia.
StadionulCeahlau.t20: Over the years the club has built up many sections (football, athletics, boxing, canoe-kayak, rowing, wrestling, amateur radio, karate) and trained generations of athletes who have represented Romania at national and international competitions.
StadionulCeahlau.t38: "Around the Ceahlăul sports complex, champions have been made, pages of sporting history have been written and a community that values movement, fair play and excellence has grown stronger."
StadionulCeahlau.t50: Discover the sporting spirit of Piatra Neamț and take the cable car for a panoramic view of the city

StrandulTineretului.t06: On the left bank of the Bistrița, the Youth Lido is the largest leisure area in Piatra Neamț and one of the most modern in Moldavia. The complex offers space for sport, relaxation and outdoor fun, and is popular with locals and visitors alike.
StrandulTineretului.t08: The area includes three swimming pools (one of them VIP), tennis, football, volleyball and basketball courts, playgrounds, holiday cabins, restaurants and terraces.
StrandulTineretului.t09: Outside the summer season, the courts and recreation areas remain open to the public.

StrandulTineretului.t14: Tennis, football, volleyball and basketball, floodlit

TeatrulTineretului.t06: The theatre that launched whole generations of artists and put Piatra Neamț on the map of Romanian theatre. The current building went up between 1929 and 1947 to plans by architect Roger Bolomey and has been used as a theatre since 1959.
TeatrulTineretului.t08: Professional work began in 1958 on the stage of the Roxy Hall, with the opening production "Scapino's Tricks" (directed by David Esrig). In 1961 it became an independent theatre, and in 1967, after a tour of West Germany, it took the name that came to define it: the Youth Theatre.
TeatrulTineretului.t18: Built with local public funds, the building was designed from the outset as a theatre and stands in the city centre, next to the Princely Court. Since 1967 the theatre has used the "2T" symbol, which became its official logo in 2007.

Telegondola.t06: Telegondola Piatra Neamț is one of the most modern and spectacular cable car systems in Romania. Opened in February 2008, it gives you a rare chance to see the city from the air, linking Piatra Neamț railway station with the top of Cozla in an 8-minute ride.
Telegondola.t08: During the ride of about 8 minutes you get spectacular views of Piatra Neamț, Lake Bâtca Doamnei, Pietricica Mountain and, on clear days, the majestic Ceahlău.
Telegondola.t13: Cozla Peak, with its leisure park and hiking trails
Telegondola.t19: Built by the Austrian company Doppelmayr, a world leader in cable transport, the cable car has 22 modern gondolas, each carrying up to 8 people.

pagina.t02: Cozla Panoramic View — accommodation on Cozla Hill, with a panoramic view over Bâtca Doamnei Lake and the city of Piatra Neamț
pagina.t05: Accommodation on Cozla Hill, in Piatra Neamț
pagina.t06: A quiet spot on the Belvedere Platform, overlooking Bâtca Doamnei Lake. Reached by gondola.
pagina.t07: Set on the Belvedere Platform, Cozla Panoramic View offers accommodation in a quiet area, with a panoramic view over Bâtca Doamnei Lake and the surroundings of the city. Access is by gondola from Piatra Neamț.
pagina.t13: The covered terrace at Cozla Panoramic View, overlooking the hills around Piatra Neamț
pagina.t16: Cozla Panoramic View sits on Cozla Hill, by the Belvedere Platform, and has {v1} simply and practically furnished rooms.
pagina.t17: The location is its main strength. From the outdoor area there is a wide view over Bâtca Doamnei Lake, the hills and the mountains around Piatra Neamț. On clear days you can even see the Ceahlău Massif in the distance.
pagina.t18: In front of the rooms there is a covered terrace and a green outdoor area where guests can spend time in the fresh air and enjoy the view.
pagina.t20: {v1} rooms for a quiet stay on Cozla
pagina.t21: The property has {v1} rooms, suited to anyone who wants to spend one or more nights on Cozla Hill.
pagina.t22: The rooms are bright and simply furnished, with practical furniture, bed linen and towels. The rooms are reached from the covered terrace.
pagina.t23: Depending on their position, some rooms look out over the surroundings and Bâtca Doamnei Lake.
pagina.t25: For availability and bookings, contact us directly on WhatsApp or fill in the form at the bottom of the page.

pagina.t33: Its position on the Belvedere Platform gives a wide view over the Piatra Neamț area.
pagina.t34: From Cozla Panoramic View you can see Bâtca Doamnei Lake, together with the hills and ridges that surround the city. The view can be enjoyed from the terrace and from the outdoor area of the property.
pagina.t35: On clear days, when visibility allows, you can also see the Ceahlău Massif in the distance.
pagina.t38: A covered terrace runs along the building, giving access to the rooms and a view of the surroundings.
pagina.t39: Beyond the terrace there is a fenced green outdoor space facing the panorama. Guests can use it to spend time outdoors during their stay.
pagina.t40: The outdoor space keeps the natural character of Cozla Hill and lets you enjoy the scenery right next to the rooms.
